method: Rebuild from primary text. Cal. Lab. Code §§1030, 1031, 1032, 1033 and 1034 were each fetched separately from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov and read in full, and the clause body was rewritten from what they say. §226.7, which §1033(a) points at for the premium, and IWC Order No. 4-2001 §12, which §1030 measures paid break time against, were also read. CourtListener was searched for decisions construing the chapter and none was found. Assertions describe the REBUILT body.
queries: Cal. Lab. Code §§1030-1034 full text, section by section (leginfo)
"Labor Code" "1030" OR "1031" lactation accommodation break time express milk employer

assertions.text: the employer must develop and implement a written policy containing four stated items
assertions.note: §1034(a)(1)-(4): the right to request accommodation, the process for making the request, the employer's obligation to respond as outlined in §1034(d), and the right to file a complaint with the Labor Commissioner. The previous body required 'a written lactation accommodation policy' and never said what has to be in it, so a policy could satisfy the clause and fail the section.

assertions.text: the policy goes in the handbook or set of policies made available to employees, and is distributed on hiring and when an employee inquires about or requests parental leave
a written response is owed whenever break time or a compliant location cannot be provided

break time is a reasonable amount each time the employee needs to express milk, runs concurrently with existing break time if possible, and is unpaid where it does not run concurrently with the wage order's authorized rest time
assertions.note: §1030, verbatim. The previous body said the break runs 'concurrently with paid rest breaks where possible' and stopped, leaving the reader to assume all of it is paid. The section says the non-concurrent part 'shall be unpaid'.

assertions.text: break time is not required where providing it would seriously disrupt the operations of the employer
assertions.note: §1032, which is one sentence long and was absent from the previous body in its entirety. This is the exception an employer reaches for first.

assertions.text: the room requirements are those in §1031(a)-(d)
assertions.note: §1031(b): not a bathroom, in close proximity to the work area, shielded from view, free from intrusion. §1031(c): safe, clean and free of hazardous materials as defined in §6382; a surface for the pump and personal items; a place to sit; access to electricity or an alternative including extension cords or charging stations. §1031(d): a sink with running water and a refrigerator in close proximity to the workspace, or another suitable cooling device if a refrigerator cannot be provided. The previous body had the surface, seating, electricity, sink and refrigeration and was missing 'shielded from view', 'free from intrusion', the cleanliness and hazard requirement, and the cooler alternative. §1031(a) also allows the normal workspace to qualify.

assertions.text: a multipurpose room may be used with lactation taking precedence while in use, and a temporary location is permitted on the same conditions
an employer with fewer than 50 employees may be exempt from a requirement on demonstrating undue hardship, and must still make reasonable efforts to provide a location other than a toilet stall
assertions.note: §1031(i), verbatim, including the definition of undue hardship as 'significant difficulty or expense when considered in relation to the size, financial resources, nature, or structure of the employer's business' and the fallback duty. This is the single most relevant qualifier in the chapter for the small employers this corpus serves and the previous body stated every requirement as absolute.

assertions.text: denial of reasonable break time OR adequate space is a failure to comply for purposes of §226.7
assertions.note: §1033(a), verbatim. The previous body said 'Denial of a required break entitles the employee to one additional hour of pay' — it dropped space, which is half the trigger.

assertions.text: the Labor Commissioner may cite and impose a civil penalty of $100 for each day an employee is denied break time or adequate space
assertions.note: §1033(c). Permissive: 'may issue a citation and may impose'. The previous body gave the §226.7 hour and stopped, so the reader saw the smaller of the two exposures.

assertions.text: the employer shall not discharge, discriminate or retaliate against an employee for exercising or attempting to exercise these rights

priorDefects: omitted: §1032 entirely — no break time is required where providing it would seriously disrupt operations.
omitted: §1031(i)'s undue-hardship exemption for employers with fewer than 50 employees, and its fallback duty.
omitted: that non-concurrent break time is unpaid (§1030).
omitted: the four required policy contents (§1034(a)).
omitted: the handbook-inclusion duty (§1034(b)) and the written-response duty (§1034(d)).
omitted: denial of adequate SPACE as a trigger for the §226.7 premium (§1033(a)).
omitted: 'shielded from view', 'free from intrusion', and the safe/clean/hazard-free requirement from the space description (§1031(b)-(c)).
gaps: No California decision construing §§1030-1034 was found on CourtListener. The chapter appears unconstrued in the published case law, so the statutory text carries the whole weight and nothing decides what 'seriously disrupt the operations of the employer' means in §1032 — which is the exception most likely to be argued.

§1031(f) (multitenant buildings and multiemployer worksites, with a two-business-day response duty on a general contractor) and §1031(g) (an agricultural employer safe harbour of a private, enclosed, shaded space) were read and are not carried. A construction or agricultural employer following this clause is being held to more than the section requires.
Whether the §226.7 premium and the §1033(c) civil penalty are both available for the same denial was not researched.

§1033(d) provides that violations of the chapter are not misdemeanours notwithstanding any other provision of the code. It was read and not carried, on the view that a compliance clause should not reassure a reader about criminal exposure it has not otherwise raised.

noCaseLawNote: CourtListener returned no decision construing Labor Code §§1030-1034. That is recorded as a finding, not as an absence of work: rule 3 of this batch required checking every section for construing case law, and the check was made and came back empty. Everything in this clause therefore rests on the statutory text alone, which is a weaker position than it looks — an unconstrued statute has not yet had its ambiguities found.
